summary: A one-line correction to the network mail meeting announced in RFC 453: the SRI-ARC meeting moves to Friday, February 23, 1973 at 8:30 AM, with Saturday as a possible second day. It is a schedule notice only.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC changes the schedule for a meeting about a network mail system. It gives the new time and place and a possible second day.

subtitle: A revised date for the Network Mail meeting announced in RFC 453.

tldr.problem: The time of the Network Mail meeting previously discussed in RFC 453 had changed.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 456 gives the revised meeting date, time, place, and possible second day.
tldr.outcome: The notice updates the meeting arrangements; it does not report meeting results.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 456's status as Unknown. The RFC updates the schedule announced in RFC 453.

sections.title: The Meeting's New Time
sections.content: RFC 456 announces a slight change to the time of the Network Mail meeting discussed in RFC 453. The revised meeting was scheduled for Friday, February 23, 1973, at 8:30 AM in the SRI-ARC Conference Room.
sections.plainLanguage: The Network Mail meeting was rescheduled. It was set for February 23 at 8:30 AM at SRI-ARC.

sections.title: A Possible Second Day
sections.content: The announcement says the group would meet on Saturday, February 24, if a second day was needed. The note does not provide an agenda or say what the participants decided.
sections.plainLanguage: If the group needed more time, it planned to meet again on Saturday. This RFC only announces the schedule.

sections.title: A Meeting Notice, Not a Mail Specification
sections.content: The RFC is a short scheduling update for a meeting about a Network Mail System. It describes no mail commands, message format, or protocol requirements.
sections.plainLanguage: This note tells readers when the meeting would take place. It does not define how network mail works.
